title: A closed scheme-theoretic union is a pushout of algebraic spaces
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Let $i:A\hookrightarrow X$ and $j:B\hookrightarrow X$ be closed subspaces [def-sfb-space-closed-subspace], with quasi-coherent ideals $\mathcal I,\mathcal J\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ under [lem-sfb-space-closed-ideal-correspondence]. Suppose $\mathcal I\cap\mathcal J=0$ as subsheaves of $\mathcal O_X$. Put $E=A\times_XB$, using sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Then the inclusions exhibit $X$ as the pushout $A\amalg_E B$ in algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Explicitly, for every algebraic space $H/S$, morphisms $f:A\to H$ and $g:B\to H$ agreeing on $E$ extend to a unique morphism $X\to H$. No Noetherian, separation or quasi-compactness hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0GFQ, lemma-pushout-fpqc-local, applied to closed unions on etale affine charts; those charts are the scheme pushouts of morphisms.tex Tag 0C4J, lemma-scheme-theoretic-union, and are algebraic-space pushouts by Tag 0EDP, lemma-pushout-along-closed-immersion-and-integral.

proof.text: Choose a representable surjective etale atlas $p:U\to X$ using [def-trf-algebraic-space]. More generally let $v:V\to X$ be any representable etale map with $V$ a scheme. Put $A_V=A\times_XV$, $B_V=B\times_XV$ and $E_V=E\times_XV$. The first two are closed subschemes of $V$ by [def-sfb-space-closed-subspace], and $E_V=A_V\times_VB_V$ by the fibre-product universal property [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Their defining ideals are the restrictions $\mathcal I_V,\mathcal J_V$ by [lem-sfb-space-closed-ideal-correspondence]. Etale pullback here is restriction on the localized small etale site [def-trf-algebraic-space]: for each etale $W\to V$, the two restricted ideals are evaluated on the same object $W\to X$. Hence their intersection is the restriction of $\mathcal I\cap\mathcal J$, and is zero. This assertion is made only for etale $v$, not for arbitrary base change.

source.place: Tag 03MB, lemma-closed-immersion-ideals, proof: restriction of the quotient structure sheaf to an etale chart.

proof.text: The scheme-theoretic union $W_V=A_V\cup B_V$ is cut out by $\mathcal I_V\cap\mathcal J_V$ by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-theoretic-union]. Since that ideal is zero, its closed inclusion identifies $W_V$ with $V$: on every affine open $\operatorname{Spec}R\subset V$ the inclusion is $\operatorname{Spec}(R/0)\to\operatorname{Spec}R$. Applying [lem-trf-closed-union-pushout] therefore makes the given cocone $A_V\leftarrow E_V\to B_V$, with vertex $V$, a pushout in schemes.

source.place: Tag 0C4J, lemma-scheme-theoretic-union: affine-local description and the cocartesian square.

proof.text: This scheme pushout is also an algebraic-space pushout by [lem-sfb-ferrand-pushout-space-agreement], as follows. Both $E_V\to A_V$ and $E_V\to B_V$ are closed immersions (base change of the closed inclusions), and the latter is integral by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-integral-separated-uc]. For any $b\in B_V$, the fibre of the closed immersion $E_V\to B_V$ has at most one underlying point. If it is nonempty, choose an affine open of $A_V$ containing the image of that point using [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis]; if empty, the empty affine open suffices. This verifies precisely the affine-neighborhood hypothesis in the cited Ferrand lemma. Thus, for the prescribed compatible $f:A\to H$, $g:B\to H$, there is a unique $h_V:V\to H$ extending their pullbacks to $A_V,B_V$, for every such scheme chart $V$. All maps are over $S$.

In particular obtain $h_U:U\to H$. The overlap $R=U\times_XU$ is a scheme and the projections $R\to U$ are etale by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] and the representable diagonal in [def-trf-algebraic-space]. The composite $R\to X$ is representable etale: on a scheme test $T\to X$, its source is $U_T\times_TU_T$, and its projection to $T$ is a composite of etale scheme maps by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation]. Apply step 3 to $R\to X$. The maps $h_U\circ\operatorname{pr}_1$ and $h_U\circ\operatorname{pr}_2$ restrict to the same maps induced by $f$ on $A_R$ and by $g$ on $B_R$; uniqueness of $h_R$ makes them equal. Now apply [lem-trf-etale-open-chart-morphism-descent] with atlas $U\to X$, invariant open $O=U$ and target $H$. Its unique descended open is all of $X$, since $X$ itself has inverse image $U$. We obtain a unique map $h:X\to H$ whose pullback to $U$ is $h_U$.

source.place: Tag 0GFQ, lemma-pushout-fpqc-local, proof: compatibility on double overlaps and descent of chart morphisms; here etale atlas descent is supplied by the cited node.

proof.text: The base-changed maps $A_U\to A$ and $B_U\to B$ are representable surjective etale scheme atlases by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. On $A_U$ the two maps $h\circ i$ and $f$ agree by construction, and on $B_U$ the maps $h\circ j$ and $g$ agree. Apply the equality-detection clause of [lem-trf-etale-open-chart-morphism-descent] with the full invariant opens $A_U$ and $B_U$ to deduce $h\circ i=f$ and $h\circ j=g$. Any other extension pulls back to $h_U$ by the local pushout uniqueness in step 3, and then equals $h$ by the same detection clause for $U\to X$. This is the claimed pushout universal property [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit].

lean.statement: theorem closed_union_isPushout {S : Scheme.{u}} (X : AlgebraicSpace S) (A B : ClosedSubspace X) (hIJ : ∀ (V : X.EtaleSite) (s : X.structureSheaf.obj.obj (op V)), (moduleStructureMap A.val.arrow).val.app (op V) s = 0 → (moduleStructureMap B.val.arrow).val.app (op V) s = 0 → s = 0) (E : AlgebraicSpace S) (a : E ⟶ (A.val : AlgebraicSpace S)) (b : E ⟶ (B.val : AlgebraicSpace S)) (hE : IsPullback a b A.val.arrow B.val.arrow) : IsPushout a b A.val.arrow B.val.arrow
lean.note: The zero intersection of the defining kernel ideals is expressed sectionwise on every object of the small etale site, avoiding a chosen complete-lattice structure on module subobjects. An arbitrary presentation of the sheaf fibre product is specified by IsPullback; IsPushout gives the full unique-extension property in algebraic spaces over S.
